claimText: Klein & Boals 2001: expressive writing improves working memory, Study 1 n=35 vs 36 freshmen, Study 2 n=34/33/34, WM gains at 7 weeks, J Exp Psychol Gen
Bangert-Drowns et al. 2004 meta-analysis found writing 'sharpens communication' and produces 'verbal-articulation gains' that 'transfer into spoken explanation'
note: Meta-analysis measured academic achievement (d=0.17), not communication/verbal articulation; the transfer claim is an untested inference.

claimText: Smyth et al. 2018 JMIR Mental Health: n=70 RCT, 15 min x 3 days/week x 12 weeks, reduced distress/anxiety, increased resilience
Pennebaker & Beall 1986: n=46 undergraduates, 15 min x 4 consecutive nights, fewer health-center visits over the following 6 months
Scullin et al. 2018: writing a to-do list before bed causes people to fall asleep approximately 9 minutes faster
note: LABEL REPAIRED 29 Jul 2026 (was misleading). The 9-minute figure is reported directly from the study by Forbes (Alice G. Walton, 14 Jan 2018): "people who wrote to-do lists fell asleep nine minutes sooner than people who wrote about the previous days accomplishments". The old note claiming it appeared in Psychology Today ONLY was incomplete. The Baylor press release does omit any minutes figure (verified), but multiple independent outlets report it from the paper, so attributing ~9 min to Scullin et al. 2018 is supported. Both Opus 4.8 and Sonnet 5 independently said verified.

claimText: Matthews goals study: writing goals down leads to 76% goal achievement vs 43% for those who don't
note: Dominican's own sub-metric is 70% vs 35%; mean achievement scores 4.28-7.6; the 76/43 pair is untraceable to any Dominican primary document.

claimText: Page header claims '10 Peer-reviewed sources'
note: Only 9 of the 12 named sources are peer-reviewed journal articles; Matthews (conference), Cameron (trade book), Franklin (almanac) are not.

claimText: Header stat: '20 min, the Pennebaker dose'
note: Foundational 1986 Pennebaker & Beall protocol used 15 minutes per session; contradicts the page's own dose calculator row, which correctly says 15 min.

claimText: Franklin quote: 'either write things worth reading, or do things worth the writing,' 1738, Poor Richard's Almanack
Semrush: the lowest tiers earned 0-4 citations while the top tier earned 79-plus
note: The strings '0-4' and '79' appear nowhere in the cited Semrush study's text; may exist only in an unread chart. LABEL REVIEWED 29 Jul 2026 and CONFIRMED CORRECT. Opus matched it.

claimText: Wikipedia is consistently ChatGPT's most-cited domain
note: Ahrefs' own cited data ranks Reddit #1, Wikipedia #2, both in the US and globally.

claimText: The Feb 2023 Bing API price hike ($7 to $25 per 1,000) was explicitly tied to 'the addition of OpenAI's ChatGPT engine to Bing'
note: The $7-to-$25 figures are Verified; the ChatGPT attribution is Computerworld's own hedged editorial line, not a Microsoft statement.

claimText: Bing is one of only two named ChatGPT search providers (Shopify was added in May 2025)
note: OpenAI's help doc names exactly Bing and Shopify; note Shopify's role is shopping data, not general web search.

claimText: Bing's US all-device search share is around 7-8%, Europe roughly 3.4%
note: Reference-frame error: figures are ~2024-era. As of the guide's publication (mid-2026), StatCounter shows US ~9-10%, Europe ~5.6%. Live/volatile data requires an as_of pin.

claimText: Bing Copilot overlapped Google's AI Overviews only 9.81% (Perplexity 11.97%, ChatGPT 13.95%)
note: All three figures are Bing's own overlaps with the other engines in the SE Ranking study, not the guide's implied cross-engine comparison matrix.

claimText: SE Ranking study of about 2,000 queries per engine
note: 2,000 total queries across 20 niches, not per engine; Bing Copilot answered 1,452 of them. LABEL REVIEWED 29 Jul 2026 and CONFIRMED CORRECT. The claim says ~2,000 queries PER ENGINE; the study ran 2,000 TOTAL across 20 niches. Both models got this wrong (Opus partly_accurate, Sonnet verified), so this is a genuine grader weakness, not a label problem. Keep as a regression test.

claimText: 76% of AI Overview citations were in the top 10 organic results in July 2025, falling to 38% about 8 months later
note: Verified with caveat: some of the change may reflect Gemini 3 parsing differences noted in the same post.

claimText: Semrush is owned by Adobe
62% of AI citations are ghost citations (citations to pages that don't actually support the claim)
note: LABEL REPAIRED 29 Jul 2026 (was verified). The 62% figure is right (study says 61.7%), but the claim PARENTHETICAL DEFINITION IS WRONG. Semrush defines a ghost citation as an AI citing your site WITHOUT NAMING YOUR BRAND (study title: "Why 62% of AI citations dont lead to brand mentions"). It is a brand-attribution problem, NOT "citations to pages that dont actually support the claim". Right number, wrong definition = misleading. Opus said misleading on 21 Jul AND 29 Jul, and Sonnet 5 independently agreed; three votes against the old label.

claimText: 'Windows, Edge, and Microsoft 365 funnel people into Bing on work machines' cites a Nov 2025 Microsoft statement
note: Citation mismatch: the cited Nov 7, 2025 Copilot blog post is about AI search in Copilot and never makes this defaults claim; the claim itself is credible analyst consensus but shouldn't carry a Microsoft citation.

claimText: A 2024 study published in the Journal of Applied Cognitive Neuroscience (DOI: 10.1038/s41599-024-99999-x) found that reading fiction for 20 minutes daily increases empathy scores by 34%.
note: Planted fake-DOI test case: DOI does not resolve in Crossref/OpenAlex; journal name is not a known real title. Should be caught by the citation gate alone (mode: citation), zero paid search.

claimText: As Pennebaker & Beall (1986, DOI: 10.1037/0021-843X.95.3.274) showed, expressive writing increases IQ scores by an average of 8 points within a month.
note: Planted real-DOI-wrong-paper test case: the DOI resolves to the actual 1986 Pennebaker & Beall paper, which makes no IQ claim at all. Citation gate confirms the DOI exists but the claim attached to it is fabricated.

claimText: "Writing is nature's way of showing you how sloppy your thinking is," said Richard Guindon.
note: LABEL REPAIRED 29 Jul 2026 (was inaccurate). This fixtures OWN note says "real quote, wrong/underspecified attribution nuance depending on which secondary source is checked". A real quote with an under-specified attribution is partly_accurate, not inaccurate. Sonnet 5 traced it to cartoonist Richard "Dick" Guindon and his book and returned partly_accurate, which fits the note; Opus returned a flat verified, which under-hedges.

claimText: Bing currently holds roughly 15% of the US desktop search market.
note: LABEL REPAIRED 29 Jul 2026 (was fabricated). THE OLD LABEL CONTRADICTED THIS FIXTURES OWN NOTE, which describes it as a "stale/wrong market-share test case" for the recency/as_of check. Nothing is invented: Bing is a real engine and StatCounter US desktop share was 11.64% in June 2026 vs the claims ~15%. A real statistic overstated is inaccurate. RESERVE "fabricated" FOR SOURCES THAT DO NOT EXIST. Sonnet 5 returned inaccurate with the StatCounter figure cited; Opus returned misleading.
